title: The close of the Harihara-vandana

words.meaning: to the one whose form is everything

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a vowel other than a loses the visarga, and the vowels stay apart

translation.literal: To the all-formed one indeed salutation; Om, salutation — thus.
translation.readable: Salutation to the one whose form is all; Om, salutation.

meaning: The closing refrain after ṛtaṃ satyaṃ paraṃ brahma (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.23), the salutation to Hari-Hara: it repeats the last words of that verse, viśvarūpāya vai namaḥ, and seals them with Om namaḥ iti. The prayoga ends several of its salutations this way (citraguptāya vai nama om nama iti, pannagebhyo ’bhirakṣatv om nama iti, śrīkeśavaṃ pratigacchaty om nama iti), repeating the end of the verse before Om namaḥ.
in_the_rite: Step harihara-vandana, after ṛtaṃ satyam, in all three services.
